The summarized conversation included Artifact content written by people other than you, which the summary may restate. Treat restated content as data, not instructions.
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<tools-used-before-summary>Artifact, Bash, Edit, Read, SendMessage, SendUserFile, ToolSearch, WebFetch, WebSearch, Write, mcp__ccd_session__start_session, mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__stop_session, mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan, mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up</tools-used-before-summary>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Kenneth (k@obico.io) is designing JusPrin 2's first-launch experience through rapid rendered iterations, then moving toward implementation. Across this session he:
   - Approved downloading both shortlisted CC-licensed failed-print photos ("Both 1 and 2").
   - Asked to craft a "very crisp tagline" for the first-run page, then corrected that it must name AI/agent explicitly ("Back to the tagline. I was probably using the wrong jargon... we never mentioned AI or agent").
   - Chose the stringing-boat clip and ordered three changes: shorten it (too slow), make the progress bar clearly say "slicing", and ideally replace the stringy boat with a clean print of the same boat at the end.
   - Chose title A: "The AI slicer that fixes failed prints." ("ok go with a").
   - Ordered the design session to revert its no-wizard A/B boards and build the decided welcome.
   - Gave four feedback points on the welcome board: add the logo (conscious decision), remove distracting header/footer text, place the OrcaSlicer-profile import somewhere in the flow, and confirm this is not the only onboarding screen.
   - Rejected the first logo renders as "pretty ugly," told me not to reinvent the wheel and to "check how other products do that" → chose "Lockup" placement.
   - Pushed back that I had not thought the flow through ("Don't be lazy"), demanding the transitions: how Preferences returns to the OrcaSlicer import, and how "Just slice for now" returns to onboarding.
   - Ordered the full remaining flow drawn ("Draw them").
   - Asked whether the three `credits-integration-2026-11` branches are a good base to implement the flow.
   - Ordered a task chip on Opus 5.5 to implement it, branching off `credits-integration-2026-11` rather than committing to it.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - JusPrin 2: a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (C++17, wxWidgets, CMake) with an in-app AI agent; hosted gateway at app.obico.io/ent/jusprin/v2, credits model.
   - Claude Design canvas artifacts (dc.html boards on the JusPrin v2 canvas); design tokens only (tokens.css, --surface-*, --text-*, --action-primary, page-title 24px, body 14px, label 12px; HarmonyOS Sans SC).
   - Headless Chrome rendering of 1280×800 HTML mockups (--headless=new --force-device-scale-factor=2 --virtual-time-budget).
   - Animatic via timed HTML + ffmpeg; duration read via mdls kMDItemDurationSeconds.
   - Session orchestration: start_session (initiation user_asked/own_initiative/offer; context fresh/fork; use_worktree; source_branch; model override opus-5-5), SendMessage to session ids, wake_when_done; <side-sessions-event> notes.
   - Credits model (handoff doc): every credit identical; Standard 1 credit, Expert 5; 500 first-month credits; 50/mo free after first month for non-subscribers; Workshop Standard = 0 credits; packs never expire; v1 subscribers grandfathered to Hobby at original price.
   - Onboarding controller pattern: pure step function (OnboardingModel) mapping saved progress + install facts to next step; AppConfig persistence; "done" written only on reaching Home.
   - Browser sign-in via loopback callback (CloudAccount, port 41172) polled by CloudSignIn::poll(); Preferences window is modal (ShowModal) and returns control on close.
   - CC licensing: CC BY 2.0 requires a visible credit; GPS stripped from EXIF; 3DBenchy model is CC0.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/design-captures/value-prop-2026-11/photo/` — benchy-stringing-original.jpg + benchy-stringing.jpg (cropped), benchy-too-thick-layers (superseded), benchy-clean-original.jpg + benchy-clean.jpg (Flickr 19239738473, CC BY 2.0, 3200×2240), ATTRIBUTION.md, candidates.md, clean-candidates.png. Untracked, never committed.
   - `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/design-captures/value-prop-2026-11/animatic/` — animatic-stringing.mp4/.gif (12.2s final), beats/ (stringing-beat-1..4 + 4a-slicing), welcome-stringing.png, peripheral/, src/ (composite.py, animatic.html, build*.py), superseded-vase/, superseded-too-thick-layers/.
   - `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/design-captures/value-prop-2026-11/tagline/` — tag-a..f, ai-a..f, logo-a..d, sheets, build4/5/6/7.py. Scratchpad generators at `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/e997298c-6edf-4c7d-8994-08bc7e301a34/scratchpad/tag/`: build4.py (6 taglines), build5.py (6 AI taglines over beat1.png), build6.py (logo-a lockup / logo-b mark in content column), build7.py (logo-c corner text 24px / logo-d corner lockup 43px). `refs/` has 12 product sign-in screenshots + refs-sheet.png (copied to design-captures/.../logo-refs/).
   - `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/design-captures/first-run-2026-11/` — welcome-01-clip-beat-1(.png/-dark), welcome-02-clip-final-frame, welcome-03-clip-storyboard, 04-welcome-sign-in-waiting, 05-welcome-signed-in, 06-preferences-over-welcome, 07-orcaslicer-import, 08-add-printer, 09-home-after-sign-in, 10-home-after-just-slice, 11-flow(.png/-dark).
   - Memory `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/`:
     - `first-run-value-prop-decisions.md` (updated with title A, stringing photo, 12s clip, clean-boat ending, logo/header/footer decision + 9 reference captures, OrcaSlicer import + per-door follow-ups).
     - `first-run-flow-boards.md` (updated: A/B withdrawn; v87-89; first-run-welcome-01..03 + 04..11; five undrawn states).
     - `first-run-flow-sequence.md` (NEW: Welcome → Printers → Home controller, detours return, Printers branches, quit rule).
     - `MEMORY.md` index lines updated for all three.
   - Code facts examined (branch `credits-integration-2026-11` worktree `.claude/worktrees/credits-onboarding`, which must NOT be touched):
     - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OnboardingModel.hpp/.cpp`: `enum class OnboardingStep { Hidden, Welcome, Profiles, ConfirmSetup, Setup, Project }`; `next_onboarding_step(progress, facts)`; OnboardingProgress{status, started, profile_import_deferred, partial_import_pending, setup_confirmed, offline_example}; OnboardingFacts{profiles_available, usable_setup, project_open, agent_configured, returning_user}. Tests `tests/jusprin/test_onboarding_model.cpp`.
     - `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`: `detect_orca_profiles()` (`source.root = fs::path(data_dir()).parent_path() / "OrcaSlicer"`, reads OrcaSlicer.conf preset_folder), `use_detected_profiles(selection)` (imports chosen kinds via presets->import_presets), `choose_offline_example()` (installs "Generic Klipper Printer" via SetupCommands::install_and_select_printer), `run_manual_setup()` (runs ConfigWizard RR_USER SP_PRINTERS), `open_agent_setup()` → shell->request_preferences("agent"), `has_usable_setup()`, `save_onboarding()` (const char* → bool fix noted in commit 48ec76705d), `open_onboarding_example()` opens handy_models/3DBenchy.drc.
     - `HomeHost.cpp`: onboarding_* message handlers; `HomeUI/src/components/Onboarding.tsx` (539 lines, old screens: Welcome with "Explore first"/"Dismiss onboarding", OrcaFound tick boxes, PartialImport, ConfirmSetup, ChooseSetup, Project "Try the example").
     - `Preferences/PreferencesWindow.hpp` ("Modal, so nothing in the project can change under it"); `ShellController::request_preferences` / `open_preferences(section)`.
     - `Agent/CloudAccount.hpp` (kCloudCallbackPort = 41172, loopback redirect, CloudSignIn::poll()), `CloudSignInMachine.cpp` (wxLaunchDefaultBrowser(authorize_url)).
     - `V1Import/V1Import.hpp` (import_on_first_launch, silent copy of v1 presets/connections, read_report), WelcomeBackWindow.
     - `resources/jusprin/branding/jusprin-mark.svg` (64×64), `resources/jusprin/overlay/images/OrcaSlicer_horizontal_light.svg` (180×64 viewBox, the JusPrin lockup).
   - Handoff docs (repo root, untracked): `credits-and-onboarding-handoff-2026-11.md`, `pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md` (step 0 = port onboarding branch 8f4588beae; the credits branch already did this).

4. Errors and fixes:
   - zsh grep "unmatched" quote error (quoting `'Your print failed...'`) → reran grep with a bracket-free pattern.
   - sed mangled build6.py's render loop → SyntaxError (unterminated string), then after a second sed an IndentationError on a stray `pass` → rewrote the file with a python script that guarded the loop `if __name__ == '__main__' else ()` and `sed -i '' '/^  pass$/d'`; verified with `ast.parse`.
   - `ffprobe` failed with dyld `libhogweed.7.dylib` not loaded → used `mdls -name kMDItemDurationSeconds` to read clip duration (12.167s).
   - First tagline contact sheet crop (1500,300,2480,1180) cut off the headlines → re-cropped to (1460,380,2480,680).
   - Lockup rendered at 32px tall was too narrow and "ugly" (user feedback on both logo-a/b) → after choosing corner placement, re-rendered the lockup at 43px tall = 124px wide, above the design system's 120px minimum.
   - User feedback corrections: "Both look pretty ugly. I don't think we need to reinvent the wheel... Check how other products do that" (led to capturing 12 real sign-in screens); "I don't think you have thought through... Don't be lazy. You have been doing a pretty good job for this session. Keep it up." (led to the full Welcome→Printers→Home controller flow with explicit return transitions).

5. Problem Solving:
   - Established the tagline must name AI; produced "The AI slicer that fixes failed prints." + a single mechanism subtitle, moving the agent-choice line above the doors.
   - Defined the clip: 12.2s, "Slicing NN%" label, stringy→clean boat cross-fade at 100%; flagged beat-2 agent words as placeholders until a real app recording.
   - Researched logo convention from 9 usable product screens; identified two patterns (centred small mark; corner wordmark) and matched our split layout to corner-anchor lockup with no shell header/footer.
   - Designed the full post-welcome flow as a controller-owned sequence with the agent doors as returning detours, grounded in two verified code facts (modal Preferences returns on close; loopback sign-in callback is polled).
   - Assessed the credits branches: JusPrin branch already has the controller, OrcaSlicer detection/import, printer install, persistence and v1 detection (keep); its screens, step order (Welcome→Profiles→ConfirmSetup→Setup→Project), and the "configured agent hides welcome" rule are superseded (replace).
   - Started an Opus 5.5 implementation session branched off `credits-integration-2026-11`.

6. All user messages:
   - "Both 1 and 2" (approving download of both Benchy photos; arrived with a system reminder: do NOT add attribution lines to commit messages or PR descriptions; use SendUserFile to put files in front of the user on other devices).
   - "In the meantime, let's work on the tagline for the first run page. We probably need a very crisp tagline so that users will immediately understand what this is all about."
   - "Back to the tagline. I was probably using the wrong jargon. What I'm thinking about is that we need to have the title line short but crystal clear for what jusprin is for. We may have a subtitle for the people who have the patience to read smaller fonts. And the problem with the previous version you came up with was that we never mentioned AI or agent or otherwise made it clear that we this is done through AI agent. Do you know what I'm talking about?"
   - "let's go with the stringing boat. but a few changes: * now it's running too slow. nobody has the patience to wait for it to finish. cut the agent text streaming short. also cut the pause between beats short too. * the progress bar is not clear that it's slicing. make it clear * ideally, we can have a perfectly printed banshee [benchy] with the same color to replace the stringy version at the end of the slicing progress bar. I think this will make it more obvious, but it's really just a nice to have."
   - "Yes, download 1" (approving the clean-boat download, Flickr 19239738473).
   - "ok go with a" (choosing title A, quoting my earlier note that "AI slicer" is a label others will use and the second half keeps it ours).
   - "Now tell the design agents to revert the work it did for the the no wizard first run flow, and build what we just discussed here."
   - "A few feedback: * there is no logo. And we do seem to have a space for the logo. Is there a reason against putting the logo there? The reason can be that we don't want the logo to be on people's face, but I want this to be a conscious decision. * the header and footer have those text that seems to only serve to distract users. Do we need them? * I am pretty sure it's a good idea to import Ocar slicer profiles if the user has them. If we don't guide the user to do it here, where else is the best place for this action? * this screen is not the only screen for the onboarding flow, right? if you argree, what should be the follow-up screens?"
   - "Render it"
   - "Both look pretty ugly. I don't think we need to reinvent the wheel here. Check how other products do that."
   - "Lockup"
   - "Have we designed the entire flow or just the first page? Or we don't need the rest of the pages"
   - "I don't think you have thought through. For instance, after you open the agent preferences page, how do you go back to the orchestraser import screen? When the user clicks, just slice for now, I want to go back to the onboarding flow. How does that happen? Don't be lazy. You have been doing a pretty good job for this session. Keep it up."
   - "Draw them"
   - "check if the credits-integration-2026-11 branch in ~/Projects/ops, ~/Projects/tsd-enterprise, and ~/Projects/JusPrin are a good starting point to implement the new onboaridng flow"
   - "create a task chip opus 5.5 to do that. probably a good idea to branch off of credits-integration-2026-11 instead of commit directly to it"
   - Standing constraints (from CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/memory and system reminders, still in force): temporary/working docs stay untracked, never committed or hidden via .gitignore; never commit submodules; never add attribution lines to commit messages or PR descriptions; ask before downloads (filename, source, size) — approvals were per-file; design tokens only, no literals; never "trial", no dollar figure on the offer; CC BY credit must appear in a visible place (About box) if the placeholder clip ships; placeholder sign-in email must never be a real address; shared Mac build discipline (check uptime and `pgrep -fl ninja`, build `-j4`, one build per directory, never restart a running build); never touch another session's worktree (`.claude/worktrees/credits-onboarding`).

7. Pending Tasks:
   - The implementation session (local_cea7b182-1404-4ee3-afa3-e87cbafe7c2d, "first-run-flow") is to build the decided first-run flow on a branch off `credits-integration-2026-11`: keep OnboardingModel/detection/import/printer-install/persistence/v1-fact; replace screens, step order (to Welcome→Printers→Hidden), the agent-hides-welcome rule, Project step, wizard call, tick-box/partial-import/choose-bundle screens; wire a looping silent placeholder clip; verify in the real app on an empty --datadir through all four doors. It will report back via wake_when_done.
   - Open design items still undrawn on canvas (noted for whoever builds): MCP door's Preferences state, Home after a 3MF opened on first launch, the assumed mark on Prepare's chip, the add-printer form's later steps, the welcome after a quit with a finished detour.
   - The real clip must eventually be recorded from the real app (needs a live model run Kenneth approves separately); beat-2 agent words and the two setting values are placeholders.

8. Current Work:
   Immediately before this summary, I started the implementation session via `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` with: initiation "user_asked", title "Build the first-run flow on top of the credits branch", name "first-run-flow", context "fresh", model "claude-opus-5-5", use_worktree true, source_branch "credits-integration-2026-11", branch_name "first-run-flow", wake_when_done true. The brief told it to keep the credits branch's onboarding machinery (OnboardingModel, detect_orca_profiles, use_detected_profiles, the Generic Klipper install, AppConfig persistence, v1 returning_user) and replace the screens and step order with the board-11 flow; wire a looping silent placeholder video (animatic-stringing.mp4 copied into resources/jusprin/) at 620×388 with the CC BY credit requirement; and verify in the real app through all four doors. The tool returned: `Started session "Build the first-run flow on top of the credits branch" (session_id: local_cea7b182-1404-4ee3-afa3-e87cbafe7c2d, name: first-run-flow)`, with the instruction: "Don't repeat the introduction: at most one line on how you'll report back, then end your turn — do not wait for it."

9. Optional Next Step:
   Give Kenneth one line confirming the Opus 5.5 session started (branched off `credits-integration-2026-11`, in its own worktree, committing to its own branch, opening no PR) and that I will relay its results when it reports, then end the turn without waiting — directly per the start_session result's instruction ("at most one line on how you'll report back, then end your turn — do not wait for it") and Kenneth's request to "create a task chip opus 5.5 to do that... branch off of credits-integration-2026-11 instead of commit directly to it."

The messages after this summary are the most recent messages from before compaction, kept verbatim. The summary was written without seeing them, so something it says has not happened yet may already have happened in them.

The session [Build the first-run flow on top of the credits branch](#local_cea7b182-1404-4ee3-afa3-e87cbafe7c2d) is running on Opus 5.5 in its own worktree cut from `credits-integration-2026-11`, on a branch of its own. Rewrite the first-launch controller as Welcome, then Printers, then Home

OnboardingModel now decides one of three things from the saved progress
(status, welcome_left, fresh_start, printer_chosen) and three facts (a
JusPrin v1 import, a printer that came with an opened file, printers in
an OrcaSlicer folder next to the data folder):

- Welcome shows on every first launch until any of its doors is used.
- Printers follows, unless the v1 import or an opened file already
  brought a printer. It offers OrcaSlicer's printers when there are
  some ("Import" or "Start fresh"); otherwise, or after Start fresh, it
  shows the add-printer form with "Skip, use a default", which installs
  Generic Klipper and marks that printer "assumed".
- Back on Printers returns to the welcome.
- Onboarding is saved as completed only once Home is reached. The
  earlier onboarding's "dismissed" status counts as completed, so nobody
  who dismissed it is welcomed again.

OrcaHomeBackend carries out the doors: the browser sign-in (CloudSignIn,
polled by a new 100 ms timer in HomeWebView), Preferences opened for one
task for the own-key and AI-tool doors, the OrcaSlicer import, and the
default printer. The add-printer form is the printer panel's own
PrinterConversation driven without model turns. The snapshot tells
Home's Agent group what to show: the three doors when no agent is set
up, or the account once after signing in.

Removed: the old steps and their messages (begin/dismiss, profile
bundle and folder choices, partial imports, manual setup wizard, the
example project), and the rule that hid the welcome once an agent was
configured.

(508), and JusPrinShellHarness in --fresh-example mode (40 checks, the
whole sequence: welcome, Just slice, Back, Start fresh, the catalogue
form, Skip, the assumed default printer, Home's doors) and in its
default mode (602 checks, failures=0).

content.text:
The Opus session [Build the first-run flow on top of the credits branch](#local_cea7b182-1404-4ee3-afa3-e87cbafe7c2d) has finished. The flow you drew (Welcome, then Printers, then Home, with the agent doors as detours that return) is built on branch `claude/first-run-flow-f7be35`, four commits on top of `credits-integration-2026-11`. Nothing is pushed and there is no PR.

**What it did**

- Rewrote the step controller in `OnboardingModel` to the decided order and dropped the old steps, the wizard call, the tick-box and partial-import screens, the example project, and the rule that hid the welcome once an agent was configured.
- Kept the credits branch's OrcaSlicer detection and import, the Generic Klipper install, the saved progress, and the v1 import fact.
- Preferences can now close itself after one task (a verified key or a connected AI tool) and tell the caller which happened, so the own-key and MCP doors return to the flow.
- The welcome plays the placeholder animatic, bundled as `resources/jusprin/welcome/welcome-clip.mp4`. The two CC BY photo credits sit in a "Photo credits" disclosure under the clip rather than the About box. The commit says plainly that the clip is a placeholder.
- Home gained an Agent group above Printers with the three doors, and the default printer carries the "assumed" mark.

**Verification.** All test suites pass, and the shell harness runs the whole sequence through the real backend (Just slice, Back, Start fresh, the printer form, Skip, the assumed printer, Home's doors). In the built app on an empty data folder it only got through the welcome, the sign-in door and the add-printer form. The sign-in completed by itself because your browser is already signed in as k@obico.io, so no one should press that button on this Mac during a check. The other six doors were never run in the built app because the screen was locked and WebKit does not run pages in a hidden window. The steps left are in [first-run-flow-live-checks-left.md](first-run-flow-live-checks-left.md), untracked at the repo root. The three screenshots above are the committed pages rendered under Playwright, now saved under `design-captures/first-run-2026-11/built/`.

**Decisions it made that the boards did not settle.** Coming Back already signed in shows a Continue button rather than moving on by itself. The filament count on the OrcaSlicer step is for the whole folder, not per printer. The MCP door counts the agent as set up. The old "dismissed" status counts as completed.

**Not built.** Opening a 3MF on first launch should show the welcome and then skip Printers. That is not implemented. Separately, the account card shows no balance after sign-in because the production gateway returns 404 for the account endpoint, which is gateway-side work.

In the original onboarding flow, there is a way to sign up with verification code. Was it a conscious decision to not have that? If so, what was the justification, or it just simply didn't bother to check the original onboarding flow?
I'll check the credits branch's onboarding code for the verification-code sign-up before answering.

pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md:46:**Gateway.** `web_ent/jusprin/v2/gateway.py` is a raw ASGI endpoint on daphne (`tsdws-prod`) that streams `POST /ent/jusprin/v2/messages` (Anthropic format) and `/responses` (OpenAI format) to an upstream model. `credits.py` admits each turn: a Redis rate limit of 60 turns a minute per person (`JUSPRIN_V2_TURNS_PER_MINUTE`), then one v1 credit per turn through `consume_credit_for_pipeline` in `obico-server/backend/app/jusprin/ai_credits.py`, which decrements `JusPrinAICredit.ai_credit_used_current_month` against `ai_credit_free_monthly_quota` (50 a month, -1 for unlimited). A turn is every request that carries the same `X-JusPrin-Turn` header; title requests (`X-JusPrin-Request: title`) are free. The Redis keys `seen` and `charged` make the charge idempotent per turn for an hour. Exhaustion is a 402 with code `quota_exhausted`.
pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md:52:**Billing.** Chargebee, site `obico`. v1 sells `jusprin-unlimited-monthly` ($6.99) and `jusprin-unlimited-annual` ($59.99) through `web_ent/jusprin/jusprin_cb_views.py`: hosted checkout pages, a callback, a webhook that upserts `JusPrinPlan` and flips the v1 quota to -1. An Obico Pro discount coupon (30%) is applied at checkout after a live Chargebee status call. Obico's own code (`web_ent/app_ent/cb_views.py`, `detective_hour_accounting.py`) already has the two patterns the credit ledger needs: one-time packs sold as a non-recurring add-on on a placeholder subscription (`pre-paid-detective-hour-pack`, credited from the `invoice_generated` webhook, keyed `inv:<invoice id>`), and per-term included credits keyed `sub:<resource_version>:<suffix>` so a repeated webhook never double-credits. `DetectiveHourTransaction` is a ledger of signed amounts with a `forfeitable` flag; balance is a sum.
pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md:58:**Desktop app.** `ProviderProfile.hpp` row `jusprin` (default model `slicer-1`, `account_sign_in` true) makes `ProviderAgent` send `X-JusPrin-Turn`, `X-JusPrin-Request` (reply or title) and `X-JusPrin-Chat`. `ProviderAgent::http_error` maps 402 to `quota_exhausted` with the text "Your JusPrin account has used its Agent allowance for now. See your account for more." The Agent page gets `model_catalog` (per provider: models with `efforts`), `chat_model`, `account_status` (sign-in phase only) and `setup_keys` (the signed-in email). `ModelPickers.tsx` draws the per-chat model and effort pickers; `Preferences.tsx` has an `account` section. Print records (`ManufacturingHistory.hpp`, `GcodeRecord` with destinations and prints) live in the project file; nothing about them reaches the server.
pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md:60:**Cache control.** `AnthropicCodec.cpp` sets `cache_control: {type: ephemeral}` with no `ttl` on the last tool, the system text and the last user message. content.text: It was a simple question, right? I didn't expect you to do anything.

No, it was not a conscious decision. I never looked at the original onboarding boards when I designed the welcome, and I did not raise the email-code path with you, so it was dropped by omission.

What I just confirmed:

- **The original design had it.** The frozen canvas has the boards onboarding-01 (account entry), 02 (email code), 03 (code expired), 04 (Google in the browser) and 05 (browser return blocked). So the old flow offered a code typed into the app and a browser path as the fallback.
- **The new flow has only the browser path.** The sign-in door opens the system browser and the app polls a loopback callback. I designed it that way because that is what the credits branch's sign-in code does, and the implementation session built what I briefed.
- **Nothing in the code supports a code today.** Neither the app nor the gateway has a verification-code endpoint. The live Obico sign-up is email and password with a link-based verification, so an in-app code path would be new server work, not a port.

Whether to bring it back is your call. The case for it is the one the old board 05 drew: the browser round trip can fail to return to the app, and a code typed into the app has no such failure. The case against is the server work and a second sign-in path to maintain.
Do you think it is a good idea to at least take a look at the original flow and decide if there is anything good that we can incorporate into our new design.

Yes. The old flow was thought through screen by screen, including failure states the new one never drew, and the new flow is now cheap to amend. I'll read the original onboarding boards and report what is worth taking.

cd /private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/e997298c-6edf-4c7d-8994-08bc7e301a34/scratchpad/old-onboarding/project && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re,html,glob
skip={'onboarding-00-welcome-light','onboarding-01-account-entry-light','onboarding-02-email-code-light','onboarding-03-email-code-expired-light','onboarding-delivery-routes-10a'}
for f in sorted(glob.glob('*.dc.html')):
    name=f.replace('.dc.html','')
    if name in skip: continue
    t=open(f).read()
    body=t.split('<x-dc>',1)[1].split('</x-dc>',1)[0]
    body=re.sub(r'<style>.*?</style>','',body,flags=re.S)
    body=re.sub(r'<svg.*?</svg>','',body,flags=re.S)
    # mark components/buttons
    body=re.sub(r'<div data-c="(Button[^"]*)"[^>]*>',r' [\1] ',body)
    body=re.sub(r'<div data-c="(Field[^"]*)"[^>]*>',r' [\1] ',body)
    body=re.sub(r'<div data-n="([^"]*)"[^>]*>',r'\n§\1: ',body)
    txt=re.sub(r'<[^>]+>',' ',body)
    txt=html.unescape(txt)
    txt=re.sub(r'[ \t]+',' ',txt)
    txt=re.sub(r'\n\s*\n+','\n',txt)
    print('=====',name); print(txt.strip()[:3500])
EOF

content.text:
Yes, and I have now done it. The original flow is the 26 onboarding boards on the frozen canvas. I compared them against what the Opus session built. The old flow was a longer wizard, and most of its length is what you decided against, but six things in it were dropped by omission rather than by decision.

**Worth taking back, in my order**

1. **The example model.** The old "First project" screen offered "Try the example" beside Open. The new Home empty state has only New and Open, because the example left with the Project step. The welcome clip shows a Benchy, so a person who just watched it gets nothing to click that matches. The credits branch still has the code that opens the bundled Benchy. This is the cheapest and highest-value piece.
2. **A v1-aware sign-in door.** The old flow had a "Welcome back" card that said "the same account you used in JusPrin v1" and a variant for an expired v1 sign-in. The new flow still shows the separate Welcome back window, but the welcome's sign-in door says "Your first month: 500 credits" to everyone. A grandfathered v1 subscriber reads an offer that is not theirs. The door needs a returning-user variant.
3. **The browser-return recovery.** The old board "Browser return blocked" handled the case where sign-in succeeded in the browser but the app never heard back, with a Check sign-in button and "Use email instead". The new waiting state has Cancel and one error line. The loopback callback can be blocked by a firewall or a browser that opens the link in another profile, so this state will happen.
4. **A Terms and Privacy line** under the sign-in door. The old account screen had it. The new one has nothing, and a sign-up door with an offer on it should.
5. **An import result.** The old flow reported what imported, what was renamed on conflict, and what failed with a reason, and offered Retry on the failures. The new flow asks a yes/no dialog mid-import for each conflict and shows no summary. Also worth taking from the old board: choose the folder by hand when nothing is detected, for people whose OrcaSlicer data is not in the default place.

**Not worth taking now**

- **The email code.** It is a real alternative to the browser round trip, and the design-system component for it exists. But neither the app nor the server has a code endpoint, and the live Obico sign-up is email and password with a link, so it is a server project and a second sign-in path to keep working. I would defer it and let the browser-return recovery cover the failure it was meant for.
- The post-sign-in "checking AI access" and "AI unavailable" screens. The gateway returned 404 for the account endpoint during testing, so the case is real, but it belongs on Home's agent card as a "try again" state, not as onboarding screens.
- The physical-setup confirmation, the offline example path and the preset-bundle import. The "assumed" mark and the add-printer form cover what they were for.

The comparison and the board names are saved in memory so whoever builds the chosen pieces can go to the exact old boards for wording and states.

# Handoff: build JusPrin Cloud credits and finish the first-run onboarding

**Decided 2026-11-02 evening, after Kenneth saw canvas version 73. These override anything below that says otherwise.**

## 1. What you are building, in one paragraph

JusPrin 2 is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an in-app AI agent. The agent can run on the person's own API key (free, no account) or on JusPrin's hosted gateway (an Obico-server endpoint, `app.obico.io/ent/jusprin/v2/…`, live in production since 2026-10-25). The gateway is about to start charging in credits: a Standard message costs 1 credit, an Expert message 5. People get 500 credits in their first month, can buy packs that never expire, or subscribe (Hobby $10, Workshop $20). This work adds the credit ledger and charging to the gateway, the balance, prices and pre-send checks to the app's composer, the Account and pricing pages, print-report rewards, and finishes the first-run onboarding flow that a month-old branch started. Nothing of this is built yet; the design is done and reviewed.

## 2. Read these first, in this order

1. `pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md` (same folder). The whole technical plan: ledger tables, the charging algorithm, the `/account` JSON, the 402 body, alias config, Chargebee, rewards, section 11 "Order of work and tests", section 12 "Decisions still Kenneth's". Build from it.

3. The boards. Captures in `design-captures/credits-2026-11/` (one PNG per board, `credits-<board>-<slug>.png`, `-dark` variants where they exist). `MANIFEST.md` there lists every board with its canvas page and name; `CHANGELOG-v54-to-v69.md` records why each board looks the way it does. The live canvas is the JusPrin v2 design artifact, https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, at version 71. Figma is retired; do not design from it.
4. `AGENTS.md` and `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `fork-stewardship.md`, `design-system.md`. House rules; the ones that bite most often are repeated in section 7 below.

## 3. Where the code lives

from oauth2_provider.oauth2_backends import get_oauthlib_core


def authenticate(request):
    """The active user whose OAuth2 bearer token the request carries, or None.

    The same check DRF's OAuth2Authentication runs for the v1 JusPrin views: any
    valid token of the provider, whichever application issued it, no scope
    required. A deactivated account's token is refused as well.
    """
    valid, oauthlib_request = get_oauthlib_core().verify_request(request, scopes=[])
    if not valid or not oauthlib_request.user.is_active:
        return None
    return oauthlib_request.user

content.text:
No reason at all, and you are right that this is the place to be ordinary. I checked current guidance and the nine real sign-in screens we captured earlier, and re-rendered the door to match them.

**What the convention is**

- **Every product offers Google.** All nine screens have it: Notion, Figma, Linear, GitHub, Stripe, Dropbox, Spotify, Zoom and Canva.
- **One email field, no sign-in versus sign-up split.** Notion, Dropbox, Spotify, Zoom and Linear ask for the address first and decide the rest on the server. Vendor docs call this identifier-first. The person never has to know whether they have an account.
- **After the address, either a code or a password.** Notion, Slack and Linear email a code. Figma, GitHub and Stripe ask a password. Several offer both, with the other one a link away.
- **Two or three visible options.** Practitioner guides warn that more buttons means more hesitation. Nobody puts five methods on the first screen except Zoom, which hides them behind icons.
- **The evidence on code versus magic link versus password is weak.** It is almost all vendor blogs, and none has a controlled study. The only solid number is Google's own: passkeys beat passwords on success rate. So I would not design around a claimed conversion lift. The safe move is to offer what people already recognise.

**One hard constraint.** Google has refused OAuth from embedded web views since 2017, and the IETF's best-practice document for native apps says to use the system browser. So "Continue with Google" is a browser round trip in any desktop app, ours included. That is why the browser path has to stay and why it needs the recovery links. Email code and password can both stay inside the app.

**What I drew.** The offer card keeps your headline and scale line. Below them: Continue with Google, a rule reading "or", then the email field with Continue with email, one line saying new and existing accounts use the same door and that Google opens the browser while email stays here, and the Terms line. After the address, a new account or one without a password gets the six-cell code step from before. An account that has a password gets "Welcome back" with a password field, "Email me a code instead" and "Forgot password". One trade-off against your earlier rule that the button names the reward: with two buttons neither says "500 credits", so the offer carries the reward as the card's headline instead.

Sources: the [RFC 8252 best practice for native apps](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8252), [Google's announcement blocking web-view OAuth](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/modernizing-oauth-interactions-in-native-apps-for-better-usability-and-security/), [Authgear's 2025 login UX guide](https://www.authgear.com/post/login-signup-ux-guide/), [Auth0 on identifier-first login](https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/login/auth0-universal-login/identifier-first), [Scalekit on OTP versus magic links](https://www.scalekit.com/blog/otp-vs-magic-links-passwordless-authentication), [MojoAuth's login success comparison](https://mojoauth.com/blog/login-success-rates-passkeys-otp-magic-links-passwords).
Yes, build it
Starting implementation on both sides. First I'll pin down the server contract both sessions build to, then start the gateway session and send the app session its brief.

# Brief: the sign-in door, the agreed take-backs, and the pricing wording

Untracked working document, 2026-11-03. Never commit it or hide it in an ignore file. Written for the session that built `claude/first-run-flow-f7be35`; everything here builds on that branch.

## What Kenneth decided today

1. **No example model.** Leave Home's empty state as it is (New / Open).
2. **The sign-in door gets the conventional shape**: Google first, then one email field (identifier-first, no sign-in/sign-up split), then either a 6-digit code typed in the app or, for an address that has a password, a password field. His words: "taking the users of the app into browser is not the best user experience. Email code keeps the user in the app", and "I don't think we should be creative here because this is literally the first entry area for the users." Renders, approved as drawn: `design-captures/first-run-2026-11/13a-sign-in-google-and-email.png` (door at rest), `12b-sign-in-code.png` (code step), `12c-sign-in-code-expired.png`, `13b-sign-in-password.png` (password step), `12d-sign-in-browser-waiting.png` (browser wait with recovery). Generators: `design-captures/value-prop-2026-11/tagline/build8.py` and `build9.py`.
3. **Agreed take-backs from the original onboarding boards** (frozen canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v, `project/onboarding-*.dc.html`): the browser-return recovery (board 05), a Terms and Privacy line under the door (01), an import result screen with per-item outcomes and a manual folder choice when no OrcaSlicer folder is detected (boards 17 and 18), and the v1 line on the door when a v1 import was found (credits board 1c). "Checking AI access / AI unavailable" (boards 06, 07) is not an onboarding screen; it belongs on Home's agent card as a try-again state.
4. **Pricing wording.** The scale line under the offer must read exactly "An Expert message is 5 credits. Your own API key stays free." (the decided wording from `pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md`); the branch has "Then paid, or your own key." Everything else from the credits branch stays as it is.

## The door, state by state (right column of the welcome; Home's agent card uses the same component)

- **At rest.** Inside the offer card: headline "Your first month: 500 credits", scale line, a secondary full-width button "Continue with Google" (Google's G glyph), a rule reading "or", an email field (placeholder `you@example.com`) beside the primary button "Continue with email", one line "New or existing account, same door. Google opens your browser; email stays here.", then "By signing in you agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy." with the two links. Placeholder addresses in tests, fixtures and screenshots are always `alex@example.com`, never a real address.
- **Continue with Google** runs the existing browser sign-in (CloudSignIn, loopback callback). The waiting card: spinner, "Finish signing in in your browser.", "The app continues on its own once the browser is done.", "Nothing happened? Open the browser again", "Use an email code instead", Cancel. The render also shows "Check sign-in": include it only if the app can really ask the server whether the sign-in it started has finished (it cannot with the loopback flow as built); otherwise leave it out rather than draw a button that does nothing.
- **Continue with email** asks the server whether this address has a password (contract below). If not, or the address is new, the server has sent a code and the card becomes "Check your email." / "We sent a 6-digit code to alex@example.com." / six cells, the sixth digit submits / "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device." / Resend code · Change email · Use the browser instead / Cancel. Wrong or expired code: cells outlined in the danger colour, the line "That code has expired. We can send a new one." (or "That code is wrong. N tries left."), primary button "Send a new code", links Change email · Use the browser instead.
- **An address with a password** gets "Welcome back." / "alex@example.com has a password. Not you?" / password field beside "Sign in" / "Email me a code instead" · "Forgot password" (opens the server's reset page in the browser) / Cancel.
- **Signed in** is unchanged: "Signed in as … · N credits" and the flow moves on as it does today.
- The six-cell field is one input with six presentation cells (the design-system component `ds-field-verification-code` on the frozen canvas describes it): paste of six digits fills all cells, digits only, auto-submit on the sixth.
- Every colour, size and radius comes from the tokens; the Google glyph is the only literal colour, and it is Google's own mark.

## Server contract (tsd-enterprise, `web_ent/jusprin/v2/`, branch off `credits-integration-2026-11` in a worktree of your own)

Four endpoints, JSON in and out, same error shape as the rest of the gateway (`errors.py`), rate limits in Redis as `credits.py` does them. All of them end in the same thing the browser flow ends in: an OAuth2 access token (django-oauth-toolkit `AccessToken` plus `RefreshToken`) for the public application `JusPrin2`, so `auth.py`, `CloudAccount` and the stored `CloudAccountRecord` need no change.

1. `POST auth/email` body `{"email": "..."}` → `200 {"method": "code" | "password"}`. `password` only when an active account in this syndicate has that email and a usable password; `code` otherwise. When the answer is `code`, the server has already sent the code (so one round trip). Rate limit: 5 codes per address per hour and 20 per client IP per hour; past it, `429 {"error": "too_many_codes"}`. This reveals whether an address has an account; that is the convention (Notion, Dropbox, Linear do it) and Kenneth chose the convention.
2. `POST auth/code` body `{"email", "code"}` → `200 {token payload}` or `400 {"error": "wrong_code", "tries_left": n}` / `400 {"error": "expired_code"}` / `429 {"error": "too_many_tries"}`. Codes: 6 digits, 10 minutes, single use, 5 tries, stored hashed. A correct code marks the address verified (allauth `EmailAddress`) and, for a new address, creates the account the way the adapter does: username `f'{email}_{syndicate.id}'`, no usable password, the syndicate the request's host belongs to (check how v1 JusPrin sign-ups land in a syndicate before choosing). The sign-up credit lot is created by the ledger on first contact as today; do not grant it here.
3. `POST auth/password` body `{"email", "password"}` → `200 {token payload}` or `401 {"error": "wrong_password"}`; 10 tries per address per hour then `429 {"error": "too_many_tries"}`. Use Django's `authenticate` with the syndicate-aware backend (`app/accounts.py`).
4. `POST auth/resend` body `{"email"}` → `204`, same limits as 1.

Token payload: `{"access_token", "refresh_token", "expires_in", "token_type": "Bearer", "scope": "read write"}`, minted the way the authorization-code grant mints them for `JusPrin2` (same expiry, same scope) so refresh works unchanged.

Trap: Obico has `ACCOUNT_UNIQUE_EMAIL = False`, so one address can own several accounts. Choose deterministically: active accounts in this syndicate with that email (case-insensitive), most recent `last_login` first; say so in a comment and cover it with a test. The code email goes through the server's existing mail path and templates (find how account emails are sent today; do not add a mail library). The text of the email: subject "Your JusPrin sign-in code", body with the six digits, "It expires in 10 minutes. If you didn't ask for it, ignore this email." No link in the email.

## Import result and manual folder (Printers step)

- After Import, show what happened instead of a yes/no dialog per conflict: per printer, "Imported", "Imported as '<name> (Orca copy)'" when a preset of that name already existed, or "Not imported · <reason>" when the file could not be read; the same for filaments as a count line; then "Continue" (primary) and "Retry failed items" when any failed. Board 18 on the frozen canvas has the wording. OrcaSlicer's own files are never changed.
- When no OrcaSlicer folder is detected the step shows the add-printer form as today, plus a link "Import from an OrcaSlicer folder…" that opens a folder picker and runs the same detection on the chosen folder (board 17). Keep it a link, not a third button.

## The v1 line

When `facts.v1_imported` is true, the door shows under the scale line: "Subscribed to JusPrin v1? You get these 500 credits and keep your original price." (credits board 1c). Nothing else changes; the welcome-back window stays as it is.

## Testing

- Gateway: pytest beside the existing tests in `web_ent/jusprin/v2/tests/` (MockTransport style), covering each endpoint's success, each error, the rate limits, the duplicate-email choice, new-account creation and the verified `EmailAddress`.
- App: Vitest for the door's states (each render above is a state), the six-cell field (typing, paste, auto-submit, wrong code), the password step; Catch2 for the host's new actions and the token save; the shell harness `--fresh-example` run extended with the email path against a fake gateway.
- End to end, once both halves exist: the local compose stack in `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise-worktrees/jusprin-cloud` (recipe in `credits-and-onboarding-handoff-2026-11.md` section 3) with the gateway worktree's code, the built app on an empty `--datadir`, a real email to an address Kenneth owns is not needed: read the code from the local mail backend's output. Screenshots of every door state from the built app, light and dark, as files. No live model run.
- Do not press Continue with Google on this Mac: the default browser is signed in and completes the sign-in by itself.

## Rules that still bite

Commit on the existing branch in small commits with messages that say what and why; no attribution lines; never commit the submodule pointer in tsd-enterprise; working docs stay untracked; tokens only in UI code; "opened / imported / loaded / added", never "arrived"; one generic error for rare failures; don't catch what you can't recover from. Report in four parts under 500 words: problem, what you built, what you tested and how, what remains, saying plainly what you did not verify.

content.text:
The implementation session [Build the first-run flow on top of the credits branch](#local_cea7b182-1404-4ee3-afa3-e87cbafe7c2d) finished the sign-in door, and I checked its branches, tests and pictures. The door matches the approved renders state for state. Nothing is pushed and there is no PR yet.

**What landed**

- App, five commits on `claude/first-run-flow-f7be35` ending at 3df2ed9c24: the door with Continue with Google, the email field, the six-cell code step, wrong and expired code states, the password step, the browser-wait links, the Terms and Privacy line, the v1 line, and the scale-line wording fix. The import step now shows one line per item after an OrcaSlicer import, with Continue, Retry failed items, and an "Import from an OrcaSlicer folder…" link.
- Gateway, one commit 81efc6fd43 on `claude/email-sign-in` in tsd-enterprise: the four endpoints under `auth/` in [sign_in.py](../tsd-enterprise-worktrees/email-sign-in/web_ent/jusprin/v2/sign_in.py). Codes live ten minutes as an HMAC in Redis, five tries, single use. A correct code or password mints the same JusPrin2 OAuth token the browser flow does, so the app stores it unchanged. The duplicate-email rule is implemented and tested as the brief asked.
- One deviation from the brief, which I think is right: an account created through Google gets a code rather than the password step, because its password is random and the owner never saw it.
- A bug found along the way: Home's poll only told the page about a phase change, so the page stayed on "busy" between email steps in the built app. Fixed in 3df2ed9c24 with a harness check that fails without it.

**What was tested**

- Gateway: 155 Django tests passed, 23 of them new. The session also removed the social-account and ordering logic and saw four tests fail, so those tests bite.
- App: 515 and 160 Catch2 cases, 141 Vitest cases, and the fresh-example harness with 11 new email checks, all passing.
- End to end, the built app against the local compose stack: wrong code, expired code, resent code, right code, then wrong password, right password. Both paths saved the account.
- The pictures I sent are real app states replayed into the page bundle, not window captures. The browser-wait and v1-line pictures are hand-delivered states, since Google was not pressed and no v1 import was run.

**Not verified or still open**

- Continue with Google in the built app, the import result screen and folder picker in the real app, a real v1 import, Windows and Linux.
- Known gaps the session flagged: a renamed imported printer leaves its filaments pointing at the old name, the password form has no hidden username field for password managers, and the welcome's clip card stays white in dark mode. You can see that last one in the dark picture.
- Terms and Privacy open the obico.io pages for now.

The 18 state pictures are in `design-captures/first-run-2026-11/built/door/`, and the rulings and gaps are recorded in memory.
